# LAN Wi-Fi Manager

> LAN Wi-Fi Manager is a free app for Windows and Ubuntu, with a macOS preview, that keeps you online when your computer is connected by both Ethernet (LAN) and Wi-Fi at the same time. It tests the internet through each adapter and, when the LAN fails or gets poor, makes Wi-Fi the preferred route, then switches back when the LAN recovers. Its Split mode can also use both lines at once: apps that follow the system proxy setting send each new connection over the LAN or the Wi-Fi, so several connections together can use both, while a single download stays on one line.

Key facts, as of 1 November 2026:

- Latest version: 2.5.0 for Windows, Ubuntu and macOS, released 2026-11-01. First public release: 1.5.0, 2026-09-25.
- Systems: Windows 10 and 11 (portable .exe, 1.9 MB, needs administrator rights, not code-signed); Ubuntu 24.04 (.deb, 8.5 MB); macOS 13.6 or later (universal .dmg, 13.7 MB, a preview that has not yet been tested on a real Mac, not signed or notarized).
- Price and licence: free for personal and work use; freeware, closed source. No ads, no paid tier, no account.
- Privacy: no telemetry. It contacts only your ping targets (8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1 by default), your adapters' DNS servers, and the GitHub API to check for updates, which can be turned off. Only if you use Split, it also asks 1.1.1.1 for each line's public address, and its speed test downloads from Cloudflare's speed test servers. Split's proxy runs on your computer and never routes traffic through an outside server.
- Limits: switching only helps when the Wi-Fi has its own route to the internet (a phone hotspot, a second provider or a separate router). Failover is one connection at a time. Split spreads new connections from proxy-aware apps over both lines; it is not bonding: a single download, call or game stays on one line, and apps that ignore the system proxy, VPNs and games are not covered. No VPN or outside server.
- Developer: bilal-nasr (https://github.com/bilal-nasr). There are no ratings, reviews or press coverage yet.

## Website

- [Home page](https://bilal-nasr.github.io/lan-wifi-manager/): what it does, how it works, screenshots, download and install notes with SHA-256 checksums, comparison with built-in options, privacy and FAQ
- [How it works](https://bilal-nasr.github.io/lan-wifi-manager/#how-it-works): the checks, the Good / Degraded / Down limits, and what it changes on each system
- [Comparison](https://bilal-nasr.github.io/lan-wifi-manager/#compare): against Windows automatic metrics, manual metrics, NetworkManager, macOS service order, a dual-WAN router and Speedify
- [Privacy](https://bilal-nasr.github.io/lan-wifi-manager/#privacy): what the app connects to and where it keeps settings and logs
- [FAQ](https://bilal-nasr.github.io/lan-wifi-manager/#faq): 12 questions, including speed of switching, SmartScreen and whether it is open source
- [Full content as Markdown](https://bilal-nasr.github.io/lan-wifi-manager/llms-full.txt): the home page and all guides in one plain Markdown file

## Guides

- [Switch from Ethernet to Wi-Fi automatically on Windows 11 and 10](https://bilal-nasr.github.io/lan-wifi-manager/guides/switch-ethernet-to-wifi-windows/): why Windows stays on a cable with no internet, interface metrics in PowerShell, the manual fix and how to undo it
- [Ubuntu: use Wi-Fi when Ethernet has no internet](https://bilal-nasr.github.io/lan-wifi-manager/guides/ubuntu-ethernet-wifi-failover/): NetworkManager route metrics, `nmcli` changes, and what the connectivity check does
- [Using Ethernet and Wi-Fi at the same time](https://bilal-nasr.github.io/lan-wifi-manager/guides/ethernet-and-wifi-at-the-same-time/): which connection is used, why speeds don't add up (and how separate connections can use both), and how to prioritise Ethernet on Windows, Ubuntu and macOS
- [All guides](https://bilal-nasr.github.io/lan-wifi-manager/guides/): index page

## Download

- [Latest release](https://github.com/bilal-nasr/lan-wifi-manager/releases/latest): release notes and all files for the current version
- [Windows 10 and 11, LanWifiManager.exe](https://github.com/bilal-nasr/lan-wifi-manager/releases/latest/download/LanWifiManager.exe): portable, 1.9 MB in 2.5.0; SmartScreen warns because it is not code-signed (More info, then Run anyway)
- [Ubuntu 24.04, LanWifiManager_2.5.0_amd64.deb](https://github.com/bilal-nasr/lan-wifi-manager/releases/download/v2.5.0/LanWifiManager_2.5.0_amd64.deb): 8.5 MB; install with `sudo apt install ./LanWifiManager_2.5.0_amd64.deb`
- [macOS 13.6 or later, LanWifiManager_2.5.0_universal.dmg](https://github.com/bilal-nasr/lan-wifi-manager/releases/download/v2.5.0/LanWifiManager_2.5.0_universal.dmg): 13.7 MB, preview; allow it under System Settings, Privacy & Security, Open Anyway
